title: The Kindly Smile
premise: Noor Zhou takes a teaching post at Hollowmere School to hide from her own past, only to find that students vanish each autumn and the town's kindness is a ritual of appeasement. When the excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside, she learns the founders bargained with something in the old well—and the contract is expiring. Refusing to sacrifice another child, Noor gathers the town's forgotten outcasts as an improvised family and completes the founders' unfinished ritual in reverse, unbinding the debt rather than renewing it. She survives by finally believing, and the town is freed at the cost of the school itself, which collapses into the refilled well.
about_author: Orsen Yarrow is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who taught for eleven years in towns too small to appear on maps. They write horror about institutions that love their people in the wrong direction.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Arriving at Hollowmere, Noor notices empty desks the staff explain with cheerful vagueness and a class photo where faces have been carefully inked out. She resolves to stay professional and invisible. The emotional beat is unease masked as routine; the chapter ends when a student, Wren, whispers that the well 'gets hungry before the frost.'

chapters.title: Sealed from the Inside
chapters.summary: POV Noor. The excavation crew unearths an iron door beneath the playground, scratched and bolted from within, and the town's warmth toward Noor turns urgent and cloying—meals, gifts, invitations. She finds the founders' ledger in the archive describing a half-finished rite of 'kindly exchange.' Beat: dread sharpening into resolve as Wren's name appears on the next page.

chapters.title: The Kindly Smile
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Wren vanishes; the town smiles through its grief, and Noor realizes the smiles are the ritual's fuel. She recruits the outcasts—the groundskeeper, the archivist's daughter, the disgraced pastor—who each carry a piece of the founders' rite. Beat: found family forged in defiance of duty, as they descend through the door before the well refills.

chapters.title: Refill
chapters.summary: POV Noor, with a closing passage from Wren. Below, Noor reverses the rite, returning what the town took and refusing the exchange, while the thing in the well wears the faces of every vanished child, smiling kindly. The school collapses into surging water; the outcasts pull her out. Beat: catharsis and grief—justice outside the law, a family that chose itself, and a town learning to grieve honestly.
